title: Base change and the unramified singular subscheme of a nodal family
statement:
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme (a scheme with a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective flat finitely presented morphism all of whose geometric fibres are nonempty connected curves of pure dimension $1$, smooth except at ordinary double points. The ordinary double point condition means that the completed local ring on a geometric fibre at a singular point is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Then the relative smooth locus $U\subset X$ is open, and there exists a closed subscheme $S_f\subset X$ with underlying set $X\setminus U$, unramified over $Y$ and with finite underlying fibres. For every morphism $Y_1\to Y$ with $Y_1$ Noetherian, the base change $f_1:X\times_Y Y_1\to Y_1$ again has all of these projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, connectedness, dimension, and nodal singularity properties. Its smooth locus is $U\times_Y Y_1$, and $S_f\times_Y Y_1$ is a closed unramified subscheme supported exactly on its nonsmooth locus. No assertion that taking the reduced closed subscheme commutes with base change is made.

Conventions for the notions used here: Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; projectivity [def-kun-projective]; flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism]; finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; geometric integrality, connectedness and reducedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]; fibre products and base change [def-pc-fibre-product]; unramified morphisms [def-weil-unramified-morphism]; closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]; dimension [def-kun-dimension].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to f. Flatness and local finite presentation are hypotheses, and every geometric fibre is a nonempty equidimensional one-dimensional fibre with at-worst-nodal singularities by the completed-local-ring assumption. The node gives the open relative smooth locus U, identifies its complement with the support of the first-Fitting singular subscheme, and proves that this singular subscheme is unramified over Y. Define S_f to be that canonical singular subscheme using [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme].

Fix a point $y\in Y$ and let $Z=S_f\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre of $S_f\to Y$; by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] its underlying space is homeomorphic to the underlying fibre of $S_f$ over $y$, so it suffices to show $Z$ has finitely many points. By step 1, $S_f\to Y$ is unramified, so $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is unramified by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open]. Since $Z=S_f\times_X X_y$ (associativity of fibre products) and $S_f\to X$ is a closed immersion, $Z\to X_y$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The fibre $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is projective by [lem-pc-projective-base-change], i.e. a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^N_{\kappa(y)}$ [def-kun-projective], hence of finite type over $\kappa(y)$ ($\mathbf P^N_{\kappa(y)}$ is covered by $N+1$ affine charts that are polynomial rings in $N$ variables, and a closed immersion is of finite type). By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-over-field-discrete] the underlying space of $Z$ is discrete, so of dimension at most zero, and [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] shows $Z$ is affine, finite over $\kappa(y)$. An affine scheme is quasi-compact, and a discrete quasi-compact space is finite. Hence every underlying fibre of $S_f\to Y$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field); Tag 02GA (base change unramified); Tag 01JY (closed immersion base change)

proof.text: For an arbitrary morphism Y_1\to Y with Y_1 Noetherian, form f_1:X\times_Y Y_1\to Y_1. Projectivity is preserved by [lem-pc-projective-base-change], flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and local finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For a geometric point of Y_1, associativity of the fibre products identifies the geometric fibre of f_1 with the geometric fibre of f over its image. Thus nonemptiness, connectedness, pure dimension one, and the completed nodal local-ring condition are inherited directly from the hypotheses on f.

Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to f_1. Its formation clause gives the scheme-theoretic equality Sing(f_1)=S_f\times_Y Y_1, while its support clause identifies the support with the nonsmooth locus of f_1. Therefore the smooth locus is U\times_Y Y_1, and S_f\times_Y Y_1 is closed and unramified over Y_1. This uses the Fitting-subsheme base-change equality itself and makes no claim about commuting reduced closed subschemes.

lean.statement: theorem projective_nodal_family_geometry {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsNoetherian Y] [IsHProjective f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hN : HasNodalGeometricFibres f) : IsOpen (f.smoothLocus : Set X) ∧ ∃ (S : Scheme.{u}) (i : S ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i ∧ (LocallyOfFiniteType (i ≫ f) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal (i ≫ f))) ∧ Set.range i = (f.smoothLocus : Set X)ᶜ ∧ (∀ y : Y, Set.Finite ((i ≫ f) ⁻¹' {y})) ∧ ∀ (Y₁ : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y₁ ⟶ Y) [IsNoetherian Y₁], IsHProjective (pullback.snd f g) ∧ Flat (pullback.snd f g) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.snd f g) ∧ HasNodalGeometricFibres (pullback.snd f g) ∧ (pullback.fst f g) ⁻¹ᵁ f.smoothLocus = (pullback.snd f g).smoothLocus ∧ IsClosedImmersion (nodalSingularBaseChangeMap f i g) ∧ (LocallyOfFiniteType (pullback.snd (i ≫ f) g) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal (pullback.snd (i ≫ f) g))) ∧ Set.range (nodalSingularBaseChangeMap f i g) = ((pullback.snd f g).smoothLocus : Set (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}))ᶜ
